To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

shift-and-persists is associated with better asthma outcomes, only among youth with asthma from families who perceive themselves to be lower in social status, and among youth who report more unfair treatment.
the links between shift-and-persists and health were moderated by perceived social standing, and by experience of unfair treatment, among youth with asthma.

shift-and-persists was associated with better profiles of asthma control and quality of life only among youth with low perceived social status or high experience of unfair treatment, suggesting that shift-and-persistent may be a particularly adaptive coping strategy for individuals who face more uncontrollable and/or stigmatizing stressors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how individuals cope with adversity, and the ways in which these coping strategies may be more or less adaptive for different people in different contexts.
the role of coping in health.
the links between coping and health, particularly among youth with chronic health conditions

the adaptive values (or lack thereof) of coping strategies depend on the family social status and the specific stressors experienced.

the adaptive values and benefits of coping strategies for individuals with low SES depend on the stressors that they are facing and on their perceived social status.
the health correlates of adaptive coping depend on the social context in which the coping occurs.
the adaptive value of coping strategies for individuals from low socioeconomic status backgrounds depends on the stressor and the social status of the individual.

the same coping strategies can be adaptive or maladaptive depending on the individual's social position.
